description: The plot illustrates how three accuracy-related metrics (Final Accuracy, Δ Accuracy, and Initial Accuracy) vary as a function of Initial Confidence. The x-axis is labeled “Initial Confidence,” uses a linear scale, and spans approximately 0.86 to 1.00 with tick labels shown at roughly 0.86, 0.88, 0.89, 0.90, … up to 1.00 (about 0.01–0.02 spacing as labeled). The y-axis is labeled “Accuracy,” uses a linear scale, and ranges from 0.0 to 1.0 with major ticks at 0.2 intervals. The Final Accuracy series is a blue solid line with circular markers and error bars, staying high across the range: it starts near about 0.92 at 0.86, rises to around 0.98–1.00 through the mid-to-high confidence region (e.g., near 0.97–0.99), and ends just under 1.0 (about 0.98–0.99) at 1.00. The Δ Accuracy series is an orange dashed line with diamond markers and error bars, starting around 0.28 at 0.86, decreasing to roughly 0.12–0.15 around 0.90–0.91, showing a local increase near 0.92 (around 0.20), then dropping to its lowest values around 0.94–0.96 (about 0.05–0.08), and finishing higher near about 0.20 at 1.00. The Initial Accuracy series is a green dashed line with square markers and error bars, beginning around 0.64 at 0.86, increasing through about 0.70–0.85 by roughly 0.88–0.91, dipping near 0.92 (around 0.78), rising to around 0.90–0.93 by about 0.94–0.96, staying near the high 0.8s to low 0.9s through about 0.99, and then dropping to roughly 0.78 at 1.00.
